Switches dithering on or off, which hides banding in gradients. With Dither on, lighting, textures and fog of 3D drawing also get noise of less than half a step of the 8 bit buffer before they are rounded to it (and before blending), so a smooth gradient in an RGBA8 buffer is a fine pattern instead of bands. It uses the same moving noise, costs a few operations per pixel, and colors that 8 bits can show exactly do not change. Blending itself stays fixed-function, so a blend of two dithered colors is rounded again. Besides that, the picture in the window gets temporal Interleaved Gradient Noise of up to half a step of the 8 bit output added when it is shown, so that the bands that rounding makes (for instance after SetGamma and UpdateGamma changed a gradient to values in between two steps) become a fine pattern that the eye averages out. The pattern moves from frame to frame (it repeats after 64 frames), which makes it average out over time as well. The noise is made on the GPU while the picture is shown, costs one pass over the screen, and does not change the buffers: ReadPixel and SaveBuffer see what was drawn (for the picture of the window; what 3D drawing made is dithered when it is drawn, so ReadPixel sees that noise). A color that the picture can show exactly stays as it is.
@param enable  True to dither, False not to. It is off by default, and unlike in the original it does not matter which color depth was asked for.
